bibl.title: Rechargeable aqueous zinc-manganese dioxide batteries with high energy and power densities

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: what actually happens at a manganese dioxide cathode in a mild-acidic aqueous zinc cell - which phase is present, which ion moves, and where the lost capacity goes
span.quote: Recently, the rechargeability of aqueous Zn-MnO2 batteries has been improved by using mild acidic electrolyte (e.g., aqueous ZnSO4 solution)−. However, the reaction mechanism of MnO2 polymorphs remains elusive and controversial. For example, electrochemical Zn-insertion in α-MnO2 is shown to undergo phase transition from tunneled structure to spinel ZnMn2O4 , layered Zn-buserite, or birnessite, most of which collapse upon cycling. A different mechanism was referred to the conversion reaction between α-MnO2 and MnOOH.

span.label: whether the competing published mechanisms for Zn insertion in MnO2 polymorphs are different reactions or one reaction seen at different points, and whether the resulting cell can be made to cycle
span.quote: Recently, the rechargeability of aqueous Zn-MnO2 batteries has been improved by using mild acidic electrolyte (e.g., aqueous ZnSO4 solution)−. However, the reaction mechanism of MnO2 polymorphs remains elusive and controversial. For example, electrochemical Zn-insertion in α-MnO2 is shown to undergo phase transition from tunneled structure to spinel ZnMn2O4 , layered Zn-buserite, or birnessite, most of which collapse upon cycling. A different mechanism was referred to the conversion reaction between α-MnO2 and MnOOH.

span.label: one common electrode mechanism for alpha, beta and gamma MnO2 - an irreversible tunnel-to-layered conversion to Zn-buserite on first discharge followed by reversible Zn2+ (de)intercalation - plus a triflate electrolyte with a Mn2+ additive giving 94% retention over 2000 cycles
span.quote: We demonstrate that the tunnel structured manganese dioxide polymorphs undergo a phase transition to layered zinc-buserite on first discharging, thus allowing subsequent intercalation of zinc cations in the latter structure. Based on this electrode mechanism, we formulate an aqueous zinc/manganese triflate electrolyte that enables the formation of a protective porous manganese oxide layer. The cathode exhibits a high reversible capacity of 225 mAh g−1 and long-term cyclability with 94% capacity retention over 2000 cycles.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We demonstrate that the tunnel structured manganese dioxide polymorphs undergo a phase transition to layered zinc-buserite on first discharging, thus allowing subsequent intercalation of zinc cations in the latter structure. Based on this electrode mechanism, we formulate an aqueous zinc/manganese triflate electrolyte that enables the formation of a protective porous manganese oxide layer. The cathode exhibits a high reversible capacity of 225 mAh g−1 and long-term cyclability with 94% capacity retention over 2000 cycles.

span.label: a cathode material that changes identity during its own first discharge, so that its measured properties before and after describe different substances
span.quote: A comparison of the crystallographic structure between β-MnO2 and Zn-buserite suggests that the co-insertion of Zn2+ and H2O and the dissolution of Mn distort the pyrolusite framework, leaving Mn vacancies in the upper/underlying layers and generating layered Zn-buserite. This tunnel-to-layer phase transition is irreversible, as indicated by the absence of EXAFS spectra recovery on first recharge.

span.label: ex-situ XRD at ten marked states across two cycles, TEM/HRTEM/ABF-STEM, EDS, XPS, TGA, synchrotron Mn K-edge XANES and EXAFS, ICP-AES on the electrolyte, three-electrode voltammetry and EIS, across four electrolyte formulations
span.term: ex-situ XRD at ten marked states across two cycles, TEM/HRTEM/ABF-STEM, EDS, XPS, TGA, synchrotron Mn K-edge XANES and EXAFS, ICP-AES on the electrolyte, three-electrode voltammetry and EIS, across four electrolyte formulations
span.quote: Notably, the XRD pattern of the rinsed cathode differs from that of previously reported species (e.g., MnOOH, spinel ZnMn2O4 , birnessite, tunneled γ-ZnMnO2 , and layered L-ZnxMnO2 ) in discharged MnO2 electrodes (Supplementary Fig. 4d). Rietveld refinement of the XRD data of the discharged electrode suggests the formation of Zn-buserite phase (Supplementary Fig. 4e).

span.label: Zn2+ and water co-insert into the pyrolusite framework, manganese dissolves away leaving vacancies, and the tunnel structure distorts into stacked layers with water between them; every subsequent cycle is intercalation into that layered product, so the material's own first discharge is the synthesis of the working electrode
span.term: a host that becomes a different host on first use
span.quote: A comparison of the crystallographic structure between β-MnO2 and Zn-buserite suggests that the co-insertion of Zn2+ and H2O and the dissolution of Mn distort the pyrolusite framework, leaving Mn vacancies in the upper/underlying layers and generating layered Zn-buserite. span.label: Mn3+ in the solid disproportionates into Mn4+ that stays and Mn2+ that leaves; pre-loading the electrolyte with Mn2+ moves the equilibrium so that less leaves, which is why an additive that is not a reactant improves retention
span.term: a dissolution equilibrium bought with a sacrificial solute
span.quote: Based on the above results, we propose three merits of the Mn2+ electrolyte additive for the Zn-MnO2 battery: (1) accommodating and compensating Mn2+ dissolution from the electrode, (2) improving initial Coulombic efficiency and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte and (3) generating a uniform porous nanostructured MnOx film on the cathode surface, which helps to maintain the electrode integrity and favor charge transfer.

span.label: charging in Mn2+-containing electrolyte electrodeposits a porous amorphous MnOx nanosheet film on the cathode; being porous it does not impede mass diffusion, and it holds the electrode together - the EIS shows a new interface resistance of 6 ohm appearing while charge transfer falls from 350 to 25
span.term: a deposit that protects rather than blocks
span.quote: Fitting the EIS data (Supplementary Table 1) gives a series resistance (R s, 4.5 Ω), an interface resistance (R i, 6.0 Ω) between electrolyte and deposited layer, a charge-transfer resistance (R ct, 25 Ω) and a Warburg diffusion impedance (Z w, 124.7 Ω). In comparison, the cell without electrolyte additive shows higher R s (8.0 Ω), R ct (350 Ω), and Z w (1200 Ω), in the absence of the apparent interface component (Fig. 6g).

span.label: triflate carries one charge against sulfate's two and is larger, so fewer water molecules surround each Zn2+; the ion moves and transfers charge more easily, which the paper offers as why the same cation in two salts gives 275 against 120 mAh g-1
span.term: a bulky anion thinning the solvation shell
span.quote: We also investigated the Zn-MnO2 cells with 3 M ZnSO4 + 0.1 M MnSO4 and 3 M Zn(CF3SO3)2 + 0.1 M MnSO4 electrolytes, which delivered initial discharge capacity of 110 and 205 mAh g−1, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 18). In SO4 2−-based electrolyte, an increase of capacity was observed within the first several cycles, which was attributed to the activation process that has been similarly found in reported α-/γ-MnO2 cathodes. Interestingly, the CF3SO3 −-based electrolyte endows much higher initial discharge capacity (275 mAh g−1 at 0.65 C) and results in capacity stabilization after ~ 10 cycles.

span.label: the exact structural motif of the Zn-buserite phase the whole mechanism rests on is not determined
span.quote: The exact structural motif of Zn-buserite is not determined yet, but will be further investigated in the future.

span.label: the tunnel-to-layer conversion is irreversible, and together with Mn dissolution and electrode pulverization it is the source of the capacity fade the additive only mitigates
span.quote: The phase tranformation, Mn dissolution and electode pulverization incur capacity fade of MnO2. By formulating an aqueous 3 M Zn(CF3SO3)2 + 0.1 M Mn(CF3SO3)2 electrolyte, the Mn2+ dissolution can be effectively accommodated and the electrode integrity can be maintained because of the in-situ generated amorphous MnOx layer.

span.label: nanorods expand and exfoliate over cycling, which the authors expect to cost capacity
span.quote: Furthermore, the TEM images of β-MnO2 electrode after different cycles (Supplementary Fig. 10) indicate expansion and exfoliation of nanorods, which is attributed to the phase transition, Mn dissolution and repeated Zn2+ intercalation, and would incur capacity loss during cycling.

span.label: the triflate salt is more expensive than the sulfate or hydroxide it replaces, and the authors say so rather than leaving it to a reader

The results suggest common electrode reaction mechanism in tunneled polymorphs of MnO2, which to the best of our knowlege, is first elucidated in mild acidic electrolytes.

The partial dissolution of Mn in electrolyte is a feasible attribution to the noticeable capacity loss on cycling.

However, similar capacity deterioration is observed upon cycling, due to the loss of active mass.

span.quote: The interesting point is that the Mn valence should increase/decrease with Zn2+ intercalation/deintercalation and would approach 3 for the fully discharged electrode, as anticipated from the discharged capacity (Fig. 2b). We postulate that such unexpected observation could be ascribed to the disproportional dissolution of trivalent Mn species (Mn3+ s → Mn4+ s + Mn2+ aq).

span.quote: The Zn-MnO2 cell was galvanostatically discharged/charged at 6.50 C (Fig. 5c) to evaluate the long-term cycling stability. Remarkably, the reversible capacity sustains 135 mAh g−1 with a capacity retention of 94% over 2000 cycles and Coulombic efficiency approaching 100%.

span.quote: Analysis of Mn by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-AES) evidences the change of Mn concentration in the electrolyte (Supplementary Fig. 11; Supplementary Note 1). On discharging, the amount of dissolved Mn increases and corresponds to ~ 8.9% of the total manganese at full discharge. The partial dissolution of Mn in electrolyte is a feasible attribution to the noticeable capacity loss on cycling.

span.label: energy density
span.quote: A stable discharge capacity of 1550 mAh can be obtained after 50 repeated cycles with an average potential of 1.35 V (Fig. 7c). The full cell delivers an energy density of 158.5 Wh kg−1 based on the total weight of the active materials (including both cathode and anode). This value far exceeds that of other aqueous Li-ion batteries (50–90 Wh kg−1) and aqueous Na-ion batteries (~ 33 Wh kg−1). Remarkably, a total energy density of 75.2 Wh kg−1 is obtained according to the mass of whole battery mass, much higher than that of commercial Pb-acid (~ 30 Wh kg−1) and Ni-Cd technologies (~ 50 Wh kg−1).

span.label: b-MnO2's capacity for zinc - AS CHARACTERISED IN THE LITERATURE: hardly any, because the (1 x 1) tunnels are too narrow to admit Zn2+

span.label: b-MnO2's capacity for zinc - AS MEASURED HERE: 307 mAh g-1 on first discharge against a theoretical 308, because the tunnels have stopped existing
span.quote: Notably, the initial discharge capacity reaches 307 mAh g−1, which approaches the theoretical capacity of 308 mAh g−1 (based on MnO2) and corresponds to 0.5 Zn2+ per MnO2.

span.term: the tunnel-to-layer conversion is irreversible, shown by EXAFS spectra that do not recover on first recharge
span.quote: A comparison of the crystallographic structure between β-MnO2 and Zn-buserite suggests that the co-insertion of Zn2+ and H2O and the dissolution of Mn distort the pyrolusite framework, leaving Mn vacancies in the upper/underlying layers and generating layered Zn-buserite. This tunnel-to-layer phase transition is irreversible, as indicated by the absence of EXAFS spectra recovery on first recharge.

span.quote: Analysis of Mn by inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometer (ICP-AES) evidences the change of Mn concentration in the electrolyte (Supplementary Fig. 11; Supplementary Note 1). On discharging, the amount of dissolved Mn increases and corresponds to ~ 8.9% of the total manganese at full discharge. The partial dissolution of Mn in electrolyte is a feasible attribution to the noticeable capacity loss on cycling.

span.label: the Mn2+ additive does three separate things - accommodates dissolution, raises efficiency and conductivity, and deposits a porous MnOx film that holds the electrode together
span.term: the Mn2+ additive does three separate things - accommodates dissolution, raises efficiency and conductivity, and deposits a porous MnOx film that holds the electrode together
span.quote: Based on the above results, we propose three merits of the Mn2+ electrolyte additive for the Zn-MnO2 battery: (1) accommodating and compensating Mn2+ dissolution from the electrode, (2) improving initial Coulombic efficiency and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte and (3) generating a uniform porous nanostructured MnOx film on the cathode surface, which helps to maintain the electrode integrity and favor charge transfer.

span.quote: A stable discharge capacity of 1550 mAh can be obtained after 50 repeated cycles with an average potential of 1.35 V (Fig. 7c). The full cell delivers an energy density of 158.5 Wh kg−1 based on the total weight of the active materials (including both cathode and anode). This value far exceeds that of other aqueous Li-ion batteries (50–90 Wh kg−1) and aqueous Na-ion batteries (~ 33 Wh kg−1). Remarkably, a total energy density of 75.2 Wh kg−1 is obtained according to the mass of whole battery mass, much higher than that of commercial Pb-acid (~ 30 Wh kg−1) and Ni-Cd technologies (~ 50 Wh kg−1).
